requirements.quote:
against this style of denial of service, endpoints that share a
   static key for stateless resets (see Section 10.3.2) MUST be arranged
   so that packets with a given connection ID always arrive at an
   instance that has connection state, unless that connection is no
   longer active.
requirements.condition: Endpoints share a static key for stateless resets, and the connection identified by a packet's connection ID remains active.
requirements.required_behavior: Arrange routing so that every packet with the given connection ID arrives at an instance that has state for that connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not route a packet for an active connection to an instance that lacks the connection state.
requirements.why_checkable: A deployment test can send packets bearing an active connection ID through all applicable routing paths and verify that each reaches an instance holding the corresponding connection state.

requirements.quote:
More generally, servers MUST NOT generate a stateless reset if a
   connection with the corresponding connection ID could be active on
   any endpoint using the same static key.
requirements.condition: A connection corresponding to the connection ID could be active on any endpoint that uses the same static key.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The server must not generate a stateless reset for that connection ID.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish or model a possibly active connection on an endpoint sharing the key, present its connection ID to the server, and verify that no stateless reset is generated.

requirements.quote:
terminated.  If there is no chance of the packet being routed to the
   correct instance, it is better to send a stateless reset than wait
   for the connection to time out.  However, this is acceptable only if
   the routing cannot be influenced by an attacker.
requirements.condition: There is no chance that the packet will be routed to the correct instance, and the implementation sends a stateless reset instead of waiting for connection timeout.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure that the routing cannot be influenced by an attacker before treating the stateless reset behavior as acceptable.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use this stateless-reset behavior when an attacker can influence the routing.
requirements.why_checkable: A routing and reset test can verify that the exceptional stateless-reset path is enabled only for routing configurations whose selection cannot be attacker-controlled.
